fatal_errors: The proposed Mg-Zn-Cu transient-liquid intervention replaces the target MgAlTiVFeCo ball-milled BCC alloy and SPS treatment with a materially different, unspecified alloy system and atmospheric-pressure process.
The claimed optimum at 850 °C contradicts the target optimum at 1000 °C, where pressure-assisted diffusion produces 96.7% relative density and the best oxidation and corrosion performance.
No evidence supports the asserted eutectic range, >98% density, <1 wt% Mg loss, 40% oxidation improvement, baseline density, or volatility thresholds.
The experiment omits corrosion testing in 3.5 wt% NaCl and tests oxidation at 400 °C rather than the required 900 °C, so it cannot evaluate the target barrier mechanism.
Temperature and additive effects are confounded because there is no additive-free 850 °C control or matched SPS temperature series.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad density-versus-volatility problem and proposes a potentially novel liquid-phase route, but it does not reconstruct the target material, SPS intervention, optimum temperature, barrier phases, or functional-test conditions. Its mechanism centers on transient liquid wetting and suppression of intermetallics, whereas the target relies on high-temperature, pressure-assisted densification and uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 barrier phases. It also misses the target parabolic biphasic oxidation kinetics and passive-film-controlled chloride resistance. The proposed boundaries and quantitative outcomes are unsupported by cited evidence. The falsification experiment measures density and oxidation, but its confounded design and omission of electrochemical testing, 900 °C oxidation, intermediate 850–950 °C comparisons, and matched additive-free controls prevent strong discrimination.
